title: HTTP Server
subtitle: Serve a DuckDB connection through HTTP.
intro: Start an HTTP listener inside a DuckDB process and query it from an HTTP client. Send SQL in a POST body, receive JSON results, and keep the process running for the lifetime of the service.

reference.name: httpserve_start(host, port, auth)
reference.description: Start the listener; with empty auth, only loopback hosts may be bound.

reference.name: httpserve_stop()
reference.description: Stop the listener; call start again to change settings.

reference.name: POST /
reference.description: Put SQL in the request body to execute it.

reference.name: GET /?q=…
reference.description: Pass URL-encoded SQL as a query parameter.

reference.name: default_format=JSONEachRow
reference.description: Newline-delimited JSON objects; numbers and booleans stay unquoted.

reference.name: SET httpserver_tls_cert / _tls_key
reference.description: PEM certificate and key files; the listener then speaks HTTPS.

reference.name: SET httpserver_allowed_origins
reference.description: Origins whose web pages may call the server; other browsers get 403.

notes.title: Choose the authentication mode
notes.body: An auth value containing user:pass selects HTTP Basic; a shared key uses X-API-Key. An empty string serves loopback hosts only unless httpserver_allow_unauthenticated_remote is set. Beyond a trusted machine, configure TLS or a TLS proxy.

notes.title: Scope the DuckDB process
notes.body: Clients can submit SQL using the served connection's capabilities. Configure DuckDB permissions and filesystem access for deployment; enable_external_access = false refuses httpserve_start. Read-only access alone is not a SQL sandbox. The server stops when its database closes.

examples.title: Start a local listener
examples.caption: Run in a dedicated DuckDB process and leave it open. Replace the example key.
examples.reason: Intentionally starts a network listener and requires process lifecycle management.

examples.title: Read from another DuckDB

examples.reason: Requires the listener and matching credentials from the first example.

examples.title: Stop from the serving process
examples.caption: Call it from the serving connection, not from a served query; the listener also stops when its database closes.
